brief.headline: A violent two-way argument about whether the Fed hikes on Sep 16, wrapped around an energy shock. The US–Iran war resumed and WTI settled at $91.48, +9.7% on the week, its strongest since mid-July, with US diesel at a record. September hike odds round-tripped from 66.1% Monday to 48.4% Thursday on Waller's "give disinflation a chance," then back to ~60–65% Friday when payrolls printed +162,000 against a +53,000 consensus. Indices went nowhere while dispersion exploded: S&P 500 7,718.60 (+0.1%), Nasdaq 26,506.99 (+0.4%), Dow 53,414.25 (−0.3%) — yet Lululemon fell 17.8% and gold dropped for a second straight week.

regime.label: Rate-constrained, not risk-off
regime.evidence: Tech, industrials and utilities held gains and the VIX closed at 14.53, yet the 30Y reached 5.28% intraweek, WTI rose 9.7% and diesel hit records — a 0.1% weekly index gain absorbing a war escalation, a 109k payroll surprise and two double-digit single-name blowups

events.title: US–Iran War Resumes and the Hormuz Supply Shock
events.reaction: WTI +9.7% to $91.48; Brent ~+7%; US diesel at an all-time record
events.detail: US forces struck IRGC targets on Sep 1 and Iran retaliated Sep 3 with missiles and drones on US bases in Kuwait and the UAE; the EU joined Operation Economic Outcast on Sep 4. The strikes spared energy infrastructure, so this is a risk-premium rebuild — with only ~4 commodity vessels crossing Hormuz Thursday against a ~15 average, and Iranian exports down from ~2m bpd pre-war to ~287k bpd.

events.title: August Payrolls — A 109k Upside Surprise
events.detail: Payrolls rose 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings +3.1% y/y, while July was revised up 44,000 to +21,000. It landed two days after ADP showed just +38,000 — a divergence that cannot both be right, and the Fed will act on the BLS number.

events.title: Broadcom Q3: AI Triples, the Guide Misses
events.reaction: AVGO fell on the guide; NVDA rose the same session — contagion absent
events.detail: Revenue rose 86% to a record $29.59bn with AI semiconductor revenue tripling to $16.7bn (+221%), and management laid out a $58bn→$115bn→$230bn AI path through 2028. But Q4 revenue guidance of ~$34.8bn missed the ~$35.03bn consensus and Q4 gross margin was guided to 73% from 78% a year earlier.

events.title: Lululemon's Tariff-Driven Guidance Slash
events.reaction: LULU −17.8% to ~$100; FY revenue guide cut by roughly $650m
events.detail: Comparable sales fell ~10% and the headline EPS beat existed only because it included $0.86/sh of tariff refunds. Management cut FY revenue guidance to $10.35–10.50bn assuming 20% tariffs from October, and excluded $105m of unrecovered IEEPA tariffs from guidance — a template other import-heavy retailers face into Q3.

events.title: Waller Signals a Hold and Hike Odds Collapse
events.detail: Governor Waller said he would be inclined to support holding rates and told markets to "give disinflation a chance," conditioning it on the Sep 11 CPI, with Williams adding that inflation expectations remain anchored. Payrolls erased the rally within 24 hours.

catalysts: August CPI · Sep 11, the condition Waller attached to his hold
FOMC decision and dot plot · Sep 15–16, priced ~60–65% for a hike
ECB Sep 10, BOJ Sep 17–18, BOE Sep 17 · synchronised tightening
Canadian retaliatory tariffs · effective Sep 8, ~$27.6bn of US goods

risks.label: The Fed hikes and equities have not priced it
Energy infrastructure, not military bases, is struck next
August CPI runs hot and Waller flips

brief.headline: The Fed's reaction function inverted. Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut on Aug 28 moved September hike odds to ~57–60% from ~35% and sent the 2-year yield up 11bp to 4.34%, lifting the dollar 0.52% to 99.67 and reversing precious metals off pre-speech highs above $4,600. Yet equities finished higher — S&P 500 7,711.76 (+0.5%), Nasdaq 26,402.42 (+0.9%), Dow 53,559.99 (+0.5%, first winning week in three) — because NVIDIA's $96.2bn quarter (+106% YoY) and ~70% FY2028 guide added ~$435–442bn of market value on Aug 27. The VIX closed near 14.4, an intraday 14.1 and its lowest of 2026, on the day the Fed signalled a hike.

regime.label: Hawkish shift equities haven't priced
regime.evidence: An 11bp front-end selloff, a +0.52% dollar and a sharp metals reversal against index gains of +0.5% to +0.9% and a VIX near a 2026 low — and on the week's best day the index rose while the average S&P constituent fell

events.title: Warsh's Hawkish Jackson Hole Debut
events.reaction: 2Y +11bp to 4.34%; Sept hike odds ~57–60%; DXY +0.52% to 99.67
events.detail: In his first Jackson Hole keynote, Chair Kevin Warsh said summer inflation prints "do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved" and that the Fed has "work to do" — signalling hikes with the funds rate at 3.50–3.75%. The debate shifted from when the Fed cuts to whether it hikes.

events.title: NVIDIA Blowout Q2 and ~70% FY2028 Guide
events.detail: Revenue hit $96.2bn, +106% YoY, with Data Center at $89.0bn (+117%) and a $108bn Q3 guide. CFO Colette Kress guided ~70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028 versus ~44% expected, though gross margin was guided to trough at 71–72% on memory costs.

events.title: "Operation Economic Outcast" — Yet Oil Fell ~5%
events.reaction: WTI ~$83.4, Brent ~$88.3, both −~5% wk into the toughest-ever Iran sanctions
events.detail: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced sweeping secondary sanctions on Iran covering digital assets, gold, aviation and shipping, designating 60 entities and vessels. Crude fell anyway as recovering Hormuz flows displaced headline risk — sanctions on revenue redirect supply rather than removing it.

events.title: The Data That Armed the Chair
events.reaction: Muted day-of (S&P −0.02% Aug 26); became the evidence base for Warsh
events.detail: July core PCE held at 3.3% YoY with headline at 3.7%, Q2 GDP was unrevised at 1.5% and claims fell to 203,000. The dissent came from the Conference Board Expectations Index at 68.2, its weakest since January and below the 80 recession threshold.

events.title: US–Canada Trade War: 50% Tariffs Meet $20bn Retaliation
events.reaction: Cited as a drag on Monday's −0.28% S&P session; otherwise absorbed
events.detail: Talks collapsed and 50% US duties took effect under Section 338 — its first-ever use — with Carney calling it a "miscalculation." Canada retaliated Aug 25 on ~$20bn of US goods, some at 50%, after the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs in February.

catalysts: August jobs report and CPI · early-to-mid September
Section 232 expansion · comment period closed Aug 27

risks.label: September hike into a complacent tape

brief.headline: The bond market stopped taking direction from the Fed and started taking it from the Treasury's balance sheet. The 30-year yield touched 5.339% on Aug 18, its highest since June 2007, as US debt crossed $40 trillion — and Treasury's surprise doubling of long-end buybacks to $4bn per operation was fully round-tripped inside 48 hours, sending the Dow down 700 points on Aug 20. The S&P 500 closed 7,674.37, −1.4%, snapping a three-week winning streak, while capital rotated into fixed-supply assets: gold ~$4,590 (+~5%), silver above $69 and bitcoin +22% to $76,943.90. Friday's flash PMI of 56.0 — the fastest US growth since April 2022, with input costs at a six-month low — supplied the counter-signal.

regime.label: Hard-asset rotation, not risk-off
regime.evidence: Equities −1.4% with defensives bid, yet VIX only 15.13 and bitcoin +22% — capital is leaving duration, not leaving risk, with gold, silver and copper all higher and the dollar at a 2.5-month low

events.title: Global duration shock — 30Y at a 19-year high, Treasury buyback intervention fails
events.reaction: 30Y hit 5.339% Aug 18; buyback rally round-tripped in 48h; Dow −700 Aug 20; S&P −1.4% on the week
events.detail: The 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.339%, its highest since June 2007, amid a synchronized global long-end selloff — UK 50-year gilt at a record 5.392%, France's 10-year at a post-2008 high, Japan's 5-year JGB at an all-time high. Treasury's Aug 19 surprise doubling of buybacks to $4bn per operation cut the 30Y 9bp for one session, then decayed entirely as the market read $4bn as immaterial against a $40tn debt stock.

events.title: Debasement trade returns as US debt tops $40 trillion
events.reaction: Gold ~$4,590 (+~5% wk, third straight gain); silver >$69; bitcoin +22% to $76,943.90; DXY to a 2.5-month low
events.detail: US national debt hit a record $40 trillion, five months after crossing $39tn, and investors read the buyback expansion as a soft form of monetization. Gold advanced alongside a rising long end — breaking the normal inverse real-rate relationship, the signature of a fiscal-credibility trade rather than a rate trade.

events.title: Hormuz deadlock — Trump vows "economic warfare" on Iran
events.reaction: WTI +6.86% to $87.06, largest weekly gain since late July; Brent $94.46, up from $88.52
events.detail: US–Iran talks deteriorated, with Tehran insisting the naval blockade must be lifted before Hormuz reopens, and Trump vowing economic warfare on Aug 20. Crude rallied nearly 7% against a larger-than-expected EIA crude build and an unexpected gasoline build — pure risk premium for a second consecutive week.

events.title: Walmart posts weakest US comps in six years, guides Q3 below consensus
events.reaction: WMT −9.5%, its worst single day since May 2022; contributed to the Dow's 700-point Aug 20 decline
events.detail: US comparable sales rose 2.6% against 3.7% expected — the slowest in more than six years — and Q3 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.62–$0.64 missed the $0.68 consensus, with management citing shoppers pressured by higher gas prices. Revenue still beat at $187.9bn, with e-commerce +23% and advertising +38%.

events.title: July FOMC minutes: 9–3 hold, "several" participants favored a hike
events.reaction: DXY fell 0.72% to a 2.5-month low on a hawkish document; September pricing settled near 30–40% hike / 60–70% hold
events.detail: The most fractured vote in years saw Hammack, Kashkari and Logan each dissent for a 25bp increase, with hawkish appetite extending beyond the three dissenters. Chair Warsh separately opened a discussion on cutting FOMC meetings from eight to six per year — an under-priced structural change that raises realized volatility around each decision.

catalysts: Nvidia Q2 FY27 earnings · Aug 26, after the close
Bessent Iran sanctions press conference · Mon Aug 24
Jackson Hole · Warsh debut keynote as Chair, Aug 28
September FOMC · Sept 16, ~30–40% hike odds priced

risks.label: Warsh hawkish surprise at Jackson Hole

brief.headline: An energy shock and a cracking consumer pulled the Fed in opposite directions, and the market decided demand wins. Crude rose 5–6% to $88.52 Brent on an open-ended US blockade of Iran — delivered despite the largest US crude build since January 2023 and OPEC's fourth straight demand downgrade, making it almost pure war premium — while soft July CPI (3.4%/2.5% core) and flat PPI cut September hike odds from ~55% to 34–38% and carried the S&P 500 to a record close of 7,798.99. Friday broke the spell: retail sales −0.6% and UMich sentiment at 51.0, yet the index still closed the week +0.4% with VIX at 14.25, its lowest close of 2026.

regime.label: Melt-up over a widening macro crack
regime.evidence: VIX at 14.25, the lowest close of 2026, and a record Russell 2000 (+3.15%) signal aggressive risk-taking, while a −0.6% consumer print, 51.0 sentiment, Dow −0.6% and Brent +5–6% signal deteriorating fundamentals underneath

events.title: Hormuz escalation — US blockade of Iran declared open-ended, tankers struck
events.reaction: Brent above $90 intraday Aug 11, closing the week at $88.52, up 5–6%; WTI ~$81–82, +5%; VIX still 14.25
events.detail: A UAV struck a tanker exiting Hormuz on Aug 14 and the UAE reported two more attacked, as Bessent announced Treasury's eighth Iran sanctions package of 2026 and Hegseth vowed an indefinite blockade of Iranian ports. The move was pure risk premium: crude rallied 5–6% in a week that delivered a +17.4mn bbl US crude build — the biggest since January 2023, against a −1.4mn draw expected — and OPEC's fourth consecutive cut to 2026 demand growth, to 580k bpd.

events.title: July CPI +0.1% m/m, 3.4% y/y; core +0.2%, 2.5% — both −0.1pp
events.reaction: September hike odds cut to 38% from 48% a day earlier; 2Y fell to 4.172%; S&P 500 closed at a record; gold above $4,400
events.detail: Headline and core annual rates each fell 0.1pp from June, with shelter up just 0.1% and accounting for roughly two-thirds of the headline increase. Arriving after the prior week's −23,000 payroll print, it was the second datapoint running to argue the Fed need not tighten into an energy shock — and it landed on a market braced the other way after three July FOMC dissents in favour of a hike, the most since September 2016.

events.title: Retail sales −0.6% and UMich sentiment collapses to 51.0
events.reaction: S&P 500 −0.2%, slipping from its record; DXY pierced 99.50 after opening near 100.00; Dow closed the week −0.6%
events.detail: Sales were $763.6bn, the biggest drop in over a year, and ex-autos was −0.3% against +0.2% expected — so not merely an auto artefact, with nonstore retailers −2.2% and motor vehicles −1.8%. UMich preliminary August sentiment then printed 51.0 against 54.5 consensus, down 8% on the month, with one-year inflation expectations at 4.3%, a fifth straight month above 4%.

events.title: Nvidia and six asset managers launch >$500bn AI financing platforms
events.reaction: NVDA gave up a morning gain to close just below flat; the intermediaries rallied instead — Apollo and KKR +6% each, Blackstone +4%
events.detail: Nvidia partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize over $500bn of third-party capital, moving AI capex off hyperscaler balance sheets into private credit and infrastructure vehicles. The split reaction is the correct read: the deal transfers financing risk to third-party capital and expands the addressable buildout without adding near-term Nvidia revenue.

events.title: July PPI flat m/m but +4.7% y/y
events.reaction: S&P 500 +0.65% to a record close of 7,798.99; 10Y −1bp to 4.6704%; CME FedWatch hike odds to ~34% from ~55% a week earlier
events.detail: Final demand was unchanged on the month with core +0.2% against +0.3% consensus, as goods −0.7% offset services +0.2% and construction +2.2%. The market took the flat headline and looked past both the 4.7% unadjusted annual rate and 9.7% year-over-year stage-1 intermediate demand — the pipeline pressure the hawks will carry into September.

catalysts: Jackson Hole, Warsh's first keynote · Aug 27–29

risks.label: Hormuz becomes a genuine supply outage
The consumer rollover is confirmed by retail guidance
Warsh signals a September hike at Jackson Hole

brief.headline: Two shocks cut the same way: Trump called off strikes on Iran and Tehran agreed Hormuz routes with Oman, taking crude down −7.8%; then July payrolls contracted 23,000 against +83,000 consensus, collapsing September hike odds from ~67% a week earlier to 40–44%. The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,757.64, its best week since April, and Nvidia gained 11.6% — but the 30Y finished at 5.192%, essentially unchanged. The market repriced the policy path without repricing the term premium.

regime.label: Clean, duration-led risk-on
regime.evidence: Nasdaq +5.19% > S&P +3.58% > Dow +2.96% in textbook beta ordering; VIX crushed from 20.66 to 14.90; HY OAS tightened to ~271bp from ~284bp, among the richest decile in its history

events.title: July payrolls −23k vs +83k est.; −103k revisions; AHE 3.2%
events.reaction: S&P record close 7,757.64; Sept hike odds ~57% → 40–44%; 10Y −7bp to 4.639%; gold +2.5%
events.detail: Payrolls fell 23,000 against +83,000 consensus on a −53,000 drop in government jobs, while May and June were revised down a combined 103,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1% only because the labour force shrank 264,000 — participation hit 61.4%, the lowest since early 2021 — and average hourly earnings slowed to 3.2% y/y, the weakest since May 2021.

events.title: Hormuz de-escalation — Iran strikes called off, Oman route deal
events.reaction: WTI −5.2% and Brent −4.7% on Aug 3; Brent −7.8% and WTI −7.6% on the week; S&P +1.48% Monday, Dow to a record close
events.detail: Trump held off planned strikes on Iran conditioned on rapidly reaching a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran then agreed proposed shipping routes with Oman, with Bessent saying a deal could land within a day. By the weekend the terms had surfaced and were not the ones Washington wanted: Iran says the agreement bars US and Israeli vessels and conditions transit on the US ending its blockade of Iranian ports.

events.title: Semiconductor / AI complex round-trips the $1T de-rating
events.reaction: Nvidia +11.6% on the week to a $5.43T market cap, its largest weekly gain in over a year; Nasdaq +5.19% vs Dow +2.96%
events.detail: The peak-capex panic that erased more than $1 trillion between July 24 and 29 reversed in five sessions, driven by UBS raising DRAM contract price forecasts to +32% for Q3 from +17%, the SpaceX–Nvidia Starmind orbital data-centre deal, and AMD's data-centre growth. The speed of the V argues the de-rating was positioning-driven rather than a real revision to the AI capex trajectory.

events.title: Earnings cluster — Palantir +29.5%, Caterpillar record, AMD beat-and-fade
events.reaction: PLTR +29.5% on +93% revenue growth; CAT +5.7% on a record $72B backlog; AMD −7% to −9% despite a record quarter; LLY +6.3%
events.detail: Palantir grew revenue 93% with US commercial up 149% and lifted FY26 guidance to $8.15bn. Caterpillar posted its first $20B+ quarter with adjusted EPS of $8.17 against $6.20 expected and power generation up 29% on data centres — the AI capex cycle now visible in industrial order books. AMD fell despite record revenue and raised guidance, on a 54% gross margin against 56% consensus.

events.title: The hawkish case that lost — ISM Mfg 55.6, Kashkari calls for a September hike
events.reaction: Held September hike odds near 55–67% into Thursday and drove the week's only risk-off session, Dow −450+ points on Aug 6
events.detail: ISM Manufacturing printed 55.6, the highest since May 2022, with employment at 52.8 — its first expansion in 33 months — while ISM Services showed Prices Paid at a hot 70.3. Kashkari, one of the three July dissenters, said he would 'rather get going now in small steps' and favoured starting as early as September. Friday's payrolls overwrote all of it; the hawkish case was postponed, not refuted.

risks.label: Hormuz deal collapses on terms the US will not accept
Hot July CPI reverses the entire week
Payroll weakness is the leading edge, not noise

brief.headline: A 9–3 FOMC hold with three dissents demanding a hike broke the tape — Dow −2.19%, its worst day since April 2025, with the 30Y at a 19-year high of 5.21% — while more than $1 trillion of global semiconductor value was erased on peak-capex fear. Indices still closed higher (S&P +1.0%, Nasdaq +1.6%) as hyperscalers rallied on the very capex killing the chipmakers, but July itself was negative for the S&P (−0.1%) and Nasdaq (−3.2%).

regime.label: Narrow risk-on over a hawkish repricing
regime.evidence: S&P +1.0% on the week but the index rose while the average stock fell; 30Y at a 19-year high, VIX spiked to 20.66; credit stayed tight (HY OAS 284bp, IG 80bp), marking a rotation rather than de-risking

events.title: FOMC holds 3.50%–3.75%, 9–3 with three dissents to hike
events.reaction: Dow −2.19% (−1,153 pts, worst since Apr 2025), S&P −1.52%; 30Y +12bp to 5.21%, a 19-year high
events.detail: Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissented for a 25bp increase — the first three-way unified dissent since September 2016. Chair Warsh said the Fed had 'missed on inflation for five years and we're going to fix that,' and the curve bear-steepened as markets moved to price a 54–70% chance of a September hike.

events.title: Iran/Hormuz — crude round-trips $100 → $88 → $90
events.reaction: Brent −8.7% Monday to $88.36; settled $90.12 Friday, −5%+ on the week but +24% in July
events.detail: Iran signalled it would suspend attacks while the US pause held, collapsing the war premium — then Trump threatened to 'hit Iran hard' and the IRGC struck two escorted tankers in the Strait on Friday. OPEC+ agreed Aug 2 to add ~188k bpd from September and then pause through Q4.

events.title: Global semiconductor / AI-hardware de-rating
events.reaction: >$1T market cap erased Jul 24–29; NVDA −$238B, SK Hynix −9.61%, Samsung −$173B, Micron −$113B
events.detail: Fears that AI infrastructure spending is peaking hit the supply chain worldwide, compounded by SK Hynix slowing HBM expansion and a Chinese breakthrough in chipmaking equipment. The week's defining paradox: hyperscalers rallied on capex guidance while chipmakers sold off on the same guidance.

events.title: Mega-cap cloud earnings — hyperscaler bifurcation
events.reaction: MSFT +8.13%, AMZN +12–15%, META −9.64%, AAPL −6% AH; MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL added ~$1.5T on the week
events.detail: Azure grew 43% and AWS 37% (fastest in 18 quarters), validating the capex spend, while Meta's identical capex raise met a 13.8% EPS miss and free cash flow of just $784M. Apple beat on EPS and revenue with iPhone +22% yet lost over $350B, days after touching a $5.0 trillion valuation.

events.title: Q2 GDP +1.5%, PCE 3.7%, ECI turns real wages negative
events.reaction: Growth missed the 1.8% consensus; core PCE sticky at 3.3% for a fourth month; yields kept rising
events.detail: GDP decelerated from 2.1% on a government-spending downturn, and the Employment Cost Index at 3.4% y/y against 3.7% PCE inflation left real wage growth at −0.4% — the first loss of purchasing power since 2022. Consumer confidence fell to 90.8 versus 92.3 expected.

risks.label: AI capex cycle confirmed as peaking
Hormuz interdiction escalates to sustained closure

brief.headline: The record run stalled as Brent crude spiked above $100/bbl (Hormuz/Red Sea escalation) collided with mega-cap earnings misses — Tesla −14% and Alphabet −7.1% reignited AI-capex fears. The S&P 500 logged its worst day since Jun 23 (−1.21% on 7/23), the Nasdaq fell ~2% on the week, VIX jumped ~11%, and the 10Y yield pushed to a multi-month high near 4.70% on tariff angst — all ahead of the Jul 28–29 FOMC.

regime.label: Cautious risk-off
regime.evidence: S&P −1.21% worst day since 6/23, Nasdaq −2% on week, VIX +~11%, 10Y at a multi-month high ~4.70%, firm safe-haven dollar

events.title: Oil shock — Hormuz/Red Sea escalation, Brent >$100
events.reaction: Brent >$100 intraday (7/23); Dow −~500 pts 7/22; risk-off
events.detail: Houthi strikes on two Saudi tankers plus a 13th straight night of US strikes on Iran near Hormuz pushed Brent above $100/bbl (+~30% m/m); it settled to ~$97 (WTI ~$92) by 7/24 as no confirmed barrels were lost.

events.title: Tesla Q2 miss + capex shock
events.reaction: TSLA −14%; dragged Nasdaq −2.15% on 7/23
events.detail: Record revenue $28.2B but adjusted EPS missed at $0.33, operating income −57%, FCF ~−$1.1B, FY capex ~$25B; TSLA fell 13–14.5% as the worst S&P 500 performer.

events.title: Broad equity risk-off + VIX spike
events.reaction: S&P −1.21% (worst since 6/23); VIX +~11%
events.detail: The oil shock plus earnings misses ended the record run; the S&P closed 7,411.98 (+0.05% Fri) after −1.21% on 7/23, the Nasdaq fell ~2% on the week, and VIX popped ~11% to ~18.6 on a semiconductor rout.

events.title: 10Y Treasury yield to multi-month high on tariffs
events.reaction: 10Y ~4.70%, 5th straight gain, highest since Jan '25
events.detail: The 10-year yield rose to ~4.69–4.70% on 7/24 — a fifth consecutive gain and highest since January 2025 — on Trump's latest tariff package, compounding tech-multiple compression.

events.title: Alphabet raises AI capex guide
events.reaction: GOOGL −7.1%; hyperscaler ROI fears
events.detail: Alphabet lifted its FY2026 capex guide to $195–205B (from $180–190B), reigniting margin/ROI concerns; GOOGL fell 7.1% on 7/23, a second leg to the mega-cap drag.

risks.label: Confirmed Hormuz/Red Sea supply loss (oil re-spike)
Hawkish FOMC surprise (hike or hawkish hold)

brief.headline: US equities pushed to fresh records — the Dow closed above 53,000 for the first time — as a June jobs miss (+57k vs ~115k) cooled hike fears; a re-escalating US–Iran conflict in the Strait of Hormuz added a ~$3–4 oil premium (WTI +~3.5%, Brent +~5%) without derailing the risk-on tape, while hawkish June FOMC minutes lifted yields and the dollar.

regime.label: Cautious risk-on

events.title: June US jobs report — sharp downside miss
events.reaction: Cooled hike bets; fueled early-week equity rally
events.detail: Payrolls rose just +57k vs ~115k consensus with −74k of prior revisions; unemployment fell to 4.2% only on lower participation — an unambiguous labor-cooling signal.

events.title: US–Iran re-escalation / Strait of Hormuz strikes
events.reaction: WTI +~3.5%, Brent +~5%; equities shrugged, closed higher
events.detail: Iran struck tankers in Hormuz (~20% of seaborne oil); Trump declared the June truce over and CENTCOM hit 80+ targets. Record UAE output capped the oil premium.

events.title: Dow tops 53,000 record / AI-led rally
events.reaction: S&P +1.8%, Nasdaq +2.1% on week; VIX to 15.84
events.detail: The Dow closed at a record 53,055.91 on Jul 6, led by Big Tech and semiconductors, extending a strong H1 (Russell 2000 +~22%, best since 1991).

events.title: FOMC June minutes — hawkish 9-8 split
events.reaction: Yields up, USD firm, gold pressured
events.detail: First minutes under Chair Kevin Warsh (rates held 3.50–3.75%) showed a 9-to-8 split on a 2026 hike, with many seeing the year-end rate above the current range.

events.title: SK Hynix record $26.5B US IPO
events.reaction: Debut +~13%; reinforced AI/HBM-memory optimism
events.detail: SK Hynix raised $26.5B on Nasdaq — the largest US listing ever by a foreign company — with demand ~7x the offer, validating AI memory-demand strength.

brief.headline: A holiday-shortened week capped a record H1 — the S&P 500 rose +14.9% and the Nasdaq +21.4% in Q2, the best quarter since 2020 — while a June jobs miss (+57k vs ~113k) was read as dovish, trimming September Fed hike odds from ~66% to ~50% and lifting gold to a record ~$4,170.

events.title: Q2/H1 2026 Record Quarter Close & Melt-Up
events.reaction: S&P Q2 +14.9%, Nasdaq +21.4%; Dow record 52,319
events.detail: Q2 closed as the best quarter since Q2 2020 (S&P +14.9%, Nasdaq +21.4%, Dow +8.9%), completing a full round-trip from the H1 energy-shock drawdown as the Iran/Hormuz shock unwound and AI/semiconductor leadership drove a melt-up.
